what: PX-2b (2026-10-20): the native training step run from a StreamPack and its ExecutionPlanV1 -- what the two artifacts cost to make (the step program as a module, K_BCIR's plan, GEM's hydration, the plan minted, both encoded), what the C lowering costs (bcir_decoder_lower_pack: the verifiers it runs, the plan's laws in one walk, GEM's dispatch twice) against the number of steps a pack carries, and what lowering inside every call costs against running the lowered program -- on the 9.84M comparison decoder (vocabulary 260, width 384, 8 heads over 4 KV heads, 6 layers, FF 1024, tied; 8 sequences of 128 tokens), every path's state the fixed sequence's, bit for bit.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 4 vCPUs: AVX-512F, no AVX512-BF16 and no AMX (the container restarted onto this host at about 03:13 UTC, after PX-2a's records were made on the AMX host), so the bf16 contract runs here without its AMX and AVX512-BF16 instances and its step is not PX-2a's; the ratios are each path's against the same trainer's other paths on this host. gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, the library at -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno; Python 3.11.15. Every record names the head it ran on (6b38768) and the first 16 hex digits of sha256(git diff HEAD -- runtime/c bcir), the new files intent-to-add: 299e73d75ee7b730, this commit's runtime/c and bcir. Wall times are indicative: one virtualized host, one process at a time.

records.pack.py: the driver of the step records: the artifacts made stage by stage, the lowering's median over 50 calls and bcir_ep_check_pack's alone, then three call paths rotated round by round on ONE trainer -- program (run_program lent the array('Q') the lowering wrote once, before the rounds), program2 (the same call again, the A/A control) and pack (run_pack: the lowering inside every call, then the same run) -- each K steps a round from one token stream; last, a second trainer that ran every one of the same calls through run (the fixed sequence), its state against the rotated one's
records.t4-bf16attnbf16.json: bf16+exp+reduce+attnbf16 at four threads: K 10, 24 rounds, 75 calls (750 steps)
records.t4-kblock.json: kblock+exp+reduce+attn (binary32) at four threads: K 10, 24 rounds, 75 calls (750 steps)
records.lower.py: the lowering's parts against K: the StreamPack's validation and laws, the plan's validation and laws, bcir_ep_check_pack and the whole lowering, each the median of 9 calls, for packs of 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 steps (binary32, one thread)

reading: No cost this host resolves for lowering a pack inside every call: pack / program reads x1.0195 (95% interval 0.997-1.042) under bf16 at four threads and x1.0037 (0.972-1.037) under binary32, beside A/A controls of x0.9979 (0.979-1.017) and x0.9923 (0.970-1.015). The lowering of a ten-step pack (2,231 claims, 1,686-1,867 values, a 423-433 KB pack and a 207-217 KB plan) takes 47.3 ms under binary32 and 54.5 ms under bf16 (the median of 50 calls), 2.1% and 1.3% of a ten-step call here (2.27 s and 4.13 s); lowered once and lent as the program arm is, a pack costs nothing per call. Its parts (lower.json, binary32, one thread, medians of 15 calls): 4.7 ms for one step, 7.2 for two, 20.2 for five, 49.6 for ten and 143.8 for twenty -- the StreamPack's validation and laws linear (2.9 ms at twenty steps, R10 linear since QUAL-LIN), the plan's laws 23.8 ms at ten and 79.8 ms at twenty: the alias law compares each lifetime with every earlier one (heap-free), the one part left quadratic. In this commit the plan walk's claim check became linear on GEM's ascending plans (QUAL-LIN's rule) and the lowering walks the plan's laws once (bcir_ep_check_pack_lifetimes): before both, the same ten-step lowering took 121 ms on this host. The artifacts take 0.34-0.37 s to make -- the step program 16 ms, the module 54-61 ms, K_BCIR's plan 28 ms, GEM's hydration 8-13 ms, the plan minted 81-109 ms, both encoded 115-181 ms -- once per state, shape and decision set. Every run's state is the reference trainer's, bit for bit, over 75 calls of ten steps. For scale against PX-2a's host (AMX, its bf16 step 67.3 ms): a 50 ms lowering is 7% of a ten-step call there if made in every call, and nothing once lowered.
